questions.q: The Receipts and Payments Account of a social club serves the same fundamental purpose as a profit-making firm's
questions.explain: A **Receipts and Payments Account** is simply a summary of the cash and bank transactions for the period. Like a **Cash Book**, it starts with an opening cash balance, records all cash received on the debit side, records all cash paid on the credit side, and ends with a closing cash balance.

questions.q: Which of the following items will appear in a Receipts and Payments Account but NOT in an Income and Expenditure Account?
options: Payment for the purchase of a new club minibus
Annual honorarium paid to the club secretary
Loss on the sale of old sports equipment
questions.explain:
The **Receipts and Payments Account** records *all* cash transactions, including capital expenditure like purchasing a minibus. 

The **Income and Expenditure Account**, however, only records *revenue* items (day-to-day running costs and incomes). The purchase of a minibus is a capital asset and goes to the Balance Sheet, not the Income and Expenditure Account. *(Note: Depreciation and loss on sale are non-cash items, so they appear in I&E but never in Receipts & Payments).*
